Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):

- single test target: tests/test_main.py

Language/layout constraints:
Keep Main.py as a thin entrypoint and put reusable modules in a lowercase snake_case package. List pytest in requirements.txt and avoid other external dependencies unless essential. Target Python 3.10 exactly: do not use typing.Self, StrEnum, exception groups, or other Python 3.11+ APIs. Design an acyclic import graph: foundational types/errors may not import engines, entrypoints, or demos; __init__.py may export only symbols actually defined by submodules.


Project-specific Python 3.10 import and deterministic-test contract:
- Main.py is a top-level module imported by pytest as from Main import run_demo; therefore Main.py MUST use absolute imports beginning with from twenty48, specifically from twenty48.game import Game and from twenty48.types import Direction, and MUST NEVER use from .twenty48, any leading-dot import, or assume the repository root is a package
- modules inside the twenty48 package may use explicit package-relative imports such as from .types import Direction; twenty48/__init__.py may re-export Board, Game, Direction, and GameStatus with package-relative imports
- expose exactly run_demo(seed: int = 0) -> dict in Main.py; it creates Game(seed), calls reset once, applies Direction.LEFT once, returns a dictionary containing status, score, and tiles, prints at most one concise line, performs no input/network/GUI work, and Main.py invokes it only under the if __name__ == "__main__": guard
- keep the canonical pure function move_line_left(line: list[int]) -> tuple[list[int], int]; it validates length four, compacts zeroes, merges each tile at most once from left to right, and reports the sum of newly merged values
- move_line_left MUST use the unambiguous output-list algorithm literally: set values=[v for v in line if v!=0] (not line[:] and not any copy retaining zeroes), output=[], score=0, i=0; while i<len(values), if i+1<len(values) and values[i]==values[i+1], append values[i]*2, add that merged value to score, and execute i+=2, otherwise append values[i] and execute i+=1; finally append zeroes until output has length four and return (output,score)
- an in-place pop algorithm is forbidden: never merge by replacing values[i] and popping values[i+1], never increment i twice after a merge, and never leave i unchanged after a merge, because either pattern skips an independent pair or lets a newly merged tile merge again in the same move
- tests/test_main.py contains exactly 2--4 concise tests and uses only absolute imports: from Main import run_demo and from twenty48.move import move_line_left; leading-dot imports and dynamically changing sys.path are forbidden
- the exact pure fixtures are move_line_left([2,2,2,0]) == ([4,2,0,0],4), move_line_left([2,2,4,4]) == ([4,8,0,0],12), and the mandatory gap-compaction fixture move_line_left([2,0,2,0]) == ([4,0,0,0],4); tests must include all three so an implementation that scans an uncompressed copy cannot pass; a smoke test calls run_demo(0) and only checks that the result is a dict with keys status, score, and tiles, avoiding brittle random-position expectations
- requirements.txt contains only a Python-3.10-compatible pytest requirement; never list the standard library or the local twenty48 package as an external dependency
- repeat the top-level absolute-import rule, forbidden leading-dot Main import, exact run_demo API, exact zero-filtering output-list merge pseudocode with i+=2/i+=1, forbidden in-place-pop and zero-retaining implementations, all three exact pure fixtures including gap compaction, and test imports in Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Test Scope Plan, Shared Knowledge, and the Main.py/twenty48/move.py/tests/test_main.py implementation tasks; merely saying that Main depends on twenty48 or that tiles merge once is insufficient

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

- runtime entry: Main.py

Keep Main.py as a thin entrypoint and put reusable modules in a lowercase snake_case package. List pytest in requirements.txt and avoid other external dependencies unless essential. Target Python 3.10 exactly: do not use typing.Self, StrEnum, exception groups, or other Python 3.11+ APIs. Design an acyclic import graph: foundational types/errors may not import engines, entrypoints, or demos; __init__.py may export only symbols actually defined by submodules.

- Main.py is a top-level module imported by pytest as from Main import run_demo; therefore Main.py MUST use absolute imports beginning with from twenty48, specifically from twenty48.game import Game and from twenty48.types import Direction, and MUST NEVER use from .twenty48, any leading-dot import, or assume the repository root is a package
- modules inside the twenty48 package may use explicit package-relative imports such as from .types import Direction; twenty48/__init__.py may re-export Board, Game, Direction, and GameStatus with package-relative imports

- keep the canonical pure function move_line_left(line: list[int]) -> tuple[list[int], int]; it validates length four, compacts zeroes, merges each tile at most once from left to right, and reports the sum of newly merged values
- move_line_left MUST use the unambiguous output-list algorithm literally: set values=[v for v in line if v!=0] (not line[:] and not any copy retaining zeroes), output=[], score=0, i=0; while i<len(values), if i+1<len(values) and values[i]==values[i+1], append values[i]*2, add that merged value to score, and execute i+=2, otherwise append values[i] and execute i+=1; finally append zeroes until output has length four and return (output,score)

- about 7 repository files

- about 650 lines of code

- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

- single-merge-per-move rule
- score accumulation
- deterministic tile spawning
- win loss and reset states

- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix

- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC

- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks

Module: twenty48.move
- def move_line_left(line: list[int]) -> tuple[list[int], int]
  Inputs:
    - line: list of length <= 4 containing non-negative integers; zeros represent empty cells. If length < 4, it will be treated as given and padded in output to length 4.
  Behavior:
    - Implements the canonical 2048 merge for a single row moving left using this exact algorithm:
      1) Create a compacted list by filtering out zeros from the input line (preserving order).
      2) Initialize i = 0 and merge_score = 0.
      3) While i < len(compacted) - 1:

      4) Create merged = [x for x in compacted if x != 0].
      5) Pad merged with zeros on the right until length is exactly 4.
    - No in-place pops are allowed; the function should use new lists for filtered/padded sequences.
  Returns:
    - (new_line, merge_score) where new_line is length 4 and merge_score is the sum of merged tile values produced in this move step.
  Purity:
    - Function is pure: no mutation of input list, no global state, no I/O.

- class Board:

    - Board must not depend on Game; only depends on Direction and move_line_left.

zeros represent empty cells. If length < 4, it will be treated as given and padded in output to length 4.\\n  Behavior:\\n    - Implements the canonical 2048 merge for a single row moving left using this exact algorithm:\\n      1) Create a compacted list by filtering out zeros from the input line (preserving order).\\n      2) Initialize i = 0 and merge_score = 0.\\n      3) While i < len(compacted) - 1:\\n         - If compacted[i] == compacted[i+1]: set compacted[i] *= 2; set compacted[i+1] = 0; increment merge_score by compacted[i]; increment i by 2.\\n         - Else: increment i by 1.\\n      4) Create merged = [x for x in compacted if x != 0].\\n      5) Pad merged with zeros on the right until length is exactly 4.\\n    - No in-place pops are allowed; the function should use new lists for filtered/padded sequences.\\n  Returns:\\n    - (new_line, merge_score) where new_line is length 4 and merge_score is the sum of merged tile values produced in this move step.\\n  Purity:\\n    - Function is pure: no mutation of input list, no global state, no I/O.\\n\\nModule: twenty48.board\\n- class Board:\\n  - grid: list[list[int]] of shape 4x4; gained_score is the total merge_score from all lines.\\n  - def can_move(self) -> bool\\n    Returns True if any cell is empty or any adjacent pair (horizontal or vertical) can merge.\\n  - def has_target(self, target: int = 2048) -> bool\\n    Returns True if any cell equals target.\\n  - def empty_positions(self) -> list[tuple[int, int]]\\n    Returns a list of (row, col) coordinates where grid[row][col] == 0, in row-major order.\\n  - def add_random_tile(self, rng: random.Random) -> bool\\n    If there are empty positions, selects one uniformly at random using rng.choice and places a tile: 2 with probability 0.9, else 4 with probability 0.1. Returns True if a tile was added, else False.\\n  Notes:\\n    - Board must not depend on Game; only depends on Direction and move_line_left.\\n\\nModule: twenty48.game\\n- class Game:\\n  - def __init__(self, seed: int = 0)\\n    Initializes Game with a deterministic random.Random seeded with seed, a Board, score=0, and status=GameStatus.RUNNING.\\n  - def reset(self) -> None\\n    Resets the Board to empty, sets score=0, status=RUNNING, and spawns exactly two tiles using add_random_tile(self.rng) twice.\\n  - def move(self, direction: Direction) -> bool\\n    If status is not RUNNING, returns False and makes no changes.\\n    Otherwise, applies Board.move(direction). If changed is True, increments score by gained_score, then:\\n      - If board.has_target(2048), set status=WON.\\n      - Else, call board.add_random_tile(self.rng). zeros represent empty cells. If length < 4, it will be treated as given and padded in output to length 4.\\n  Behavior:\\n    - Implements the canonical 2048 merge for a single row moving left using this exact algorithm:\\n      1) Create a compacted list by filtering out zeros from the input line (preserving order).\\n      2) Initialize i = 0 and merge_score = 0.\\n      3) While i < len(compacted) - 1:\\n         - If compacted[i] == compacted[i+1]: set compacted[i] *= 2; set compacted[i+1] = 0; increment merge_score by compacted[i]; increment i by 2.\\n         - Else: increment i by 1.\\n      4) Create merged = [x for x in compacted if x != 0].\\n      5) Pad merged with zeros on the right until length is exactly 4.\\n    - No in-place pops are allowed; the function should use new lists for filtered/padded sequences.\\n  Returns:\\n    - (new_line, merge_score) where new_line is length 4 and merge_score is the sum of merged tile values produced in this move step.\\n  Purity:\\n    - Function is pure: no mutation of input list, no global state, no I/O.\\n\\nModule: twenty48.board\\n- class Board:\\n  - grid: list[list[int]] of shape 4x4; gained_score is the total merge_score from all lines.\\n  - def can_move(self) -> bool\\n    Returns True if any cell is empty or any adjacent pair (horizontal or vertical) can merge.\\n  - def has_target(self, target: int = 2048) -> bool\\n    Returns True if any cell equals target.\\n  - def empty_positions(self) -> list[tuple[int, int]]\\n    Returns a list of (row, col) coordinates where grid[row][col] == 0, in row-major order.\\n  - def add_random_tile(self, rng: random.Random) -> bool\\n    If there are empty positions, selects one uniformly at random using rng.choice and places a tile: 2 with probability 0.9, else 4 with probability 0.1. Generate a complete medium-size Python 3.10 repository architecture for: 2048 game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: requirements.txt
- runtime entry: Main.py
- single test target: tests/test_main.py
- test command: python -m pytest -q
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Keep Main.py as a thin entrypoint and put reusable modules in a lowercase snake_case package. List pytest in requirements.txt and avoid other external dependencies unless essential. Target Python 3.10 exactly: do not use typing.Self, StrEnum, exception groups, or other Python 3.11+ APIs. Design an acyclic import graph: foundational types/errors may not import engines, entrypoints, or demos; __init__.py may export only symbols actually defined by submodules.


Project-specific Python 3.10 import and deterministic-test contract:
- Main.py is a top-level module imported by pytest as from Main import run_demo; therefore Main.py MUST use absolute imports beginning with from twenty48, specifically from twenty48.game import Game and from twenty48.types import Direction, and MUST NEVER use from .twenty48, any leading-dot import, or assume the repository root is a package
- modules inside the twenty48 package may use explicit package-relative imports such as from .types import Direction; twenty48/__init__.py may re-export Board, Game, Direction, and GameStatus with package-relative imports
- expose exactly run_demo(seed: int = 0) -> dict in Main.py; it creates Game(seed), calls reset once, applies Direction.LEFT once, returns a dictionary containing status, score, and tiles, prints at most one concise line, performs no input/network/GUI work, and Main.py invokes it only under the if __name__ == "__main__": guard
- keep the canonical pure function move_line_left(line: list[int]) -> tuple[list[int], int]; it validates length four, compacts zeroes, merges each tile at most once from left to right, and reports the sum of newly merged values
- move_line_left MUST use the unambiguous output-list algorithm literally: set values=[v for v in line if v!=0] (not line[:] and not any copy retaining zeroes), output=[], score=0, i=0; while i<len(values), if i+1<len(values) and values[i]==values[i+1], append values[i]*2, add that merged value to score, and execute i+=2, otherwise append values[i] and execute i+=1; finally append zeroes until output has length four and return (output,score)
- an in-place pop algorithm is forbidden: never merge by replacing values[i] and popping values[i+1], never increment i twice after a merge, and never leave i unchanged after a merge, because either pattern skips an independent pair or lets a newly merged tile merge again in the same move
- tests/test_main.py contains exactly 2--4 concise tests and uses only absolute imports: from Main import run_demo and from twenty48.move import move_line_left; leading-dot imports and dynamically changing sys.path are forbidden
- the exact pure fixtures are move_line_left([2,2,2,0]) == ([4,2,0,0],4), move_line_left([2,2,4,4]) == ([4,8,0,0],12), and the mandatory gap-compaction fixture move_line_left([2,0,2,0]) == ([4,0,0,0],4); tests must include all three so an implementation that scans an uncompressed copy cannot pass; a smoke test calls run_demo(0) and only checks that the result is a dict with keys status, score, and tiles, avoiding brittle random-position expectations
- requirements.txt contains only a Python-3.10-compatible pytest requirement; never list the standard library or the local twenty48 package as an external dependency
- repeat the top-level absolute-import rule, forbidden leading-dot Main import, exact run_demo API, exact zero-filtering output-list merge pseudocode with i+=2/i+=1, forbidden in-place-pop and zero-retaining implementations, all three exact pure fixtures including gap compaction, and test imports in Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Test Scope Plan, Shared Knowledge, and the Main.py/twenty48/move.py/tests/test_main.py implementation tasks; merely saying that Main depends on twenty48 or that tiles merge once is insufficient


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 33 functions or methods
- about 650 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- 4x4 board
- left right up and down moves
- single-merge-per-move rule
- score accumulation
- deterministic tile spawning
- win loss and reset states

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Module: twenty48.move
- def move_line_left(line: list[int]) -> tuple[list[int], int]
  Inputs:
    - line: list of length <= 4 containing non-negative integers; zeros represent empty cells. If length < 4, it will be treated as given and padded in output to length 4.
  Behavior:
    - Implements the canonical 2048 merge for a single row moving left using this exact algorithm:
      1) Create a compacted list by filtering out zeros from the input line (preserving order).
      2) Initialize i = 0 and merge_score = 0.
      3) While i < len(compacted) - 1:
         - If compacted[i] == compacted[i+1]: set compacted[i] *= 2; set compacted[i+1] = 0; increment merge_score by compacted[i]; increment i by 2.

      4) Create merged = [x for x in compacted if x != 0].
      5) Pad merged with zeros on the right until length is exactly 4.
    - No in-place pops are allowed; the function should use new lists for filtered/padded sequences.
  Returns:
    - (new_line, merge_score) where new_line is length 4 and merge_score is the sum of merged tile values produced in this move step.

Module: twenty48.move
- def move_line_left(line: list[int]) -> tuple[list[int], int]
  Inputs:
    - line: list of length <= 4 containing non-negative integers; zeros represent empty cells. If length < 4, it will be treated as given and padded in output to length 4.
  Behavior:
    - Implements the canonical 2048 merge for a single row moving left using this exact algorithm:
      1) Create a compacted list by filtering out zeros from the input line (preserving order).
      2) Initialize i = 0 and merge_score = 0.
      3) While i < len(compacted) - 1:
         - If compacted[i] == compacted[i+1]: set compacted[i] *= 2; set compacted[i+1] = 0; increment merge_score by compacted[i]; increment i by 2.
         - Else: increment i by 1.
      4) Create merged = [x for x in compacted if x != 0].
      5) Pad merged with zeros on the right until length is exactly 4.
    - No in-place pops are allowed; the function should use new lists for filtered/padded sequences.
  Returns:
    - (new_line, merge_score) where new_line is length 4 and merge_score is the sum of merged tile values produced in this move step.
  Purity:
    - Function is pure: no mutation of input list, no global state, no I/O.

Module: twenty48.board
- class Board:
  - grid: list[list[int]] of shape 4x4; integers >= 0; 0 denotes empty.
  - def get_grid(self) -> list[list[int]]
    Returns a deep copy or safe-to-read copy of the 4x4 grid suitable for inspection in tests or by Game.
  - def reset_empty(self) -> None
    Sets grid to all zeros (4x4).
  - def move(self, direction: Direction) -> tuple[bool, int]
    Applies a move in the given direction to the board.
    Uses twenty48.move.move_line_left on each row/column, transforming rows/columns as needed for RIGHT/UP/DOWN by reversing or transposing.
    Returns (changed, gained_score) where changed is True if any tile moved or merged; gained_score is the total merge_score from all lines.
  - def can_move(self) -> bool
    Returns True if any cell is empty or any adjacent pair (horizontal or vertical) can merge.
  - def has_target(self, target: int = 2048) -> bool
    Returns True if any cell equals target.
  - def empty_positions(self) -> list[tuple[int, int]]
    Returns a list of (row, col) coordinates where grid[row][col] == 0, in row-major order.
  - def add_random_tile(self, rng: random.Random) -> bool
    If there are empty positions, selects one uniformly at random using rng.choice and places a tile: 2 with probability 0.9, else 4 with probability 0.1. Returns True if a tile was added, else False.

    - Board must not depend on Game; only depends on Direction and move_line_left.

- class Game:

Module: twenty48.move
- def move_line_left(line: list[int]) -> tuple[list[int], int]
  Inputs:
    - line: list of length <= 4 containing non-negative integers; zeros represent empty cells. If length < 4, it will be treated as given and padded in output to length 4.

    - (new_line, merge_score) where new_line is length 4 and merge_score is the sum of merged tile values produced in this move step.

    - Function is pure: no mutation of input list, no global state, no I/O.

    If there are empty positions, selects one uniformly at random using rng.choice and places a tile: 2 with probability 0.9, else 4 with probability 0.1. Returns True if a tile was added, else False.

    - Board must not depend on Game; only depends on Direction and move_line_left.

Generate a complete medium-size Python 3.10 repository architecture for: 2048 game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: requirements.txt
- runtime entry: Main.py
- single test target: tests/test_main.py
- test command: python -m pytest -q
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Keep Main.py as a thin entrypoint and put reusable modules in a lowercase snake_case package. List pytest in requirements.txt and avoid other external dependencies unless essential. Target Python 3.10 exactly: do not use typing.Self, StrEnum, exception groups, or other Python 3.11+ APIs. Design an acyclic import graph: foundational types/errors may not import engines, entrypoints, or demos; __init__.py may export only symbols actually defined by submodules.


Project-specific Python 3.10 import and deterministic-test contract:
- Main.py is a top-level module imported by pytest as from Main import run_demo; therefore Main.py MUST use absolute imports beginning with from twenty48, specifically from twenty48.game import Game and from twenty48.types import Direction, and MUST NEVER use from .twenty48, any leading-dot import, or assume the repository root is a package
- modules inside the twenty48 package may use explicit package-relative imports such as from .types import Direction; twenty48/__init__.py may re-export Board, Game, Direction, and GameStatus with package-relative imports
- expose exactly run_demo(seed: int = 0) -> dict in Main.py; it creates Game(seed), calls reset once, applies Direction.LEFT once, returns a dictionary containing status, score, and tiles, prints at most one concise line, performs no input/network/GUI work, and Main.py invokes it only under the if __name__ == "__main__": guard
- keep the canonical pure function move_line_left(line: list[int]) -> tuple[list[int], int]; it validates length four, compacts zeroes, merges each tile at most once from left to right, and reports the sum of newly merged values
- move_line_left MUST use the unambiguous output-list algorithm literally: set values=[v for v in line if v!=0] (not line[:] and not any copy retaining zeroes), output=[], score=0, i=0; while i<len(values), if i+1<len(values) and values[i]==values[i+1], append values[i]*2, add that merged value to score, and execute i+=2, otherwise append values[i] and execute i+=1; finally append zeroes until output has length four and return (output,score)
- an in-place pop algorithm is forbidden: never merge by replacing values[i] and popping values[i+1], never increment i twice after a merge, and never leave i unchanged after a merge, because either pattern skips an independent pair or lets a newly merged tile merge again in the same move
- tests/test_main.py contains exactly 2--4 concise tests and uses only absolute imports: from Main import run_demo and from twenty48.move import move_line_left; leading-dot imports and dynamically changing sys.path are forbidden
- the exact pure fixtures are move_line_left([2,2,2,0]) == ([4,2,0,0],4), move_line_left([2,2,4,4]) == ([4,8,0,0],12), and the mandatory gap-compaction fixture move_line_left([2,0,2,0]) == ([4,0,0,0],4); tests must include all three so an implementation that scans an uncompressed copy cannot pass; a smoke test calls run_demo(0) and only checks that the result is a dict with keys status, score, and tiles, avoiding brittle random-position expectations
- requirements.txt contains only a Python-3.10-compatible pytest requirement; never list the standard library or the local twenty48 package as an external dependency
- repeat the top-level absolute-import rule, forbidden leading-dot Main import, exact run_demo API, exact zero-filtering output-list merge pseudocode with i+=2/i+=1, forbidden in-place-pop and zero-retaining implementations, all three exact pure fixtures including gap compaction, and test imports in Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Test Scope Plan, Shared Knowledge, and the Main.py/twenty48/move.py/tests/test_main.py implementation tasks; merely saying that Main depends on twenty48 or that tiles merge once is insufficient


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 33 functions or methods
- about 650 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- 4x4 board
- left right up and down moves
- single-merge-per-move rule
- score accumulation
- deterministic tile spawning
- win loss and reset states

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents
